channel.title: Griffin Kozlowski: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Griffin Kozlowski: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends

item.title: KITTIE’s Comeback Wasn’t Planned, Says MERCEDES LANDER: 'We Just Wanted To Play A Couple Shows'
item.description: Canadian metal band KITTIE is back with a new album, but the comeback wasn’t part of a grand plan. In a recent interview with Loud TV (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), drummer Mercedes Lander explained how the return came together almost by accident.

item.title: EVANESCENCE Hits No. 1 on Rock Chart for the First Time With 'Afterlife'
item.description: Evanescence has reached a major milestone. The band has scored its first-ever No. 1 song on Billboard’s Mainstream Rock Airplay chart with “Afterlife”, their latest single featured in the Netflix series Devil May Cry (watch below).

item.title: DEFTONES Tease Possible NEW SONG Or ALBUM Release With Cryptic Message During London Show
item.description: Deftones may be getting ready to release new music. During their concert at Crystal Palace Park in London on June 29, the band displayed a graphic on large screens near the stage.

item.title: The Song JAMES HETFIELD Considers the Greatest of All, and Countless Bands Have Tried to Recreate
item.description: James Hetfield has always worn his influences on his sleeve. In a recent episode of The Metallica Report (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), the Metallica frontman named Led Zeppelin’s “Stairway to Heaven” as the greatest song of all time.

item.title: GENE HOGLAN Says METALLICA’s 'One' Echoes DARK ANGEL: 'That Beat Came From Us'
item.description: In a recent interview, Gene Hoglan, drummer for the thrash metal band Dark Angel, shared his thoughts on a long-standing theory among metal fans, that Metallica’s 1988 track “One” was inspired by Dark Angel’s 1986 song “Darkness Descends.

item.title: HALESTORM Releases New Music Video for 'DARKNESS ALWAYS WINS': 'Evil Prevails And The Good Depart First'
item.description: Halestorm has unveiled a new official video for “Darkness Always Wins,” the band’s first release of 2025 (watch it below). Directed by DJay Brawner and produced by Dave Cobb, the song builds slowly with a cinematic tone and sits firmly in the band’s hard rock catalog.

item.title: Why IRON MAIDEN Turned To Japan Before Chasing The American Dream, According to ROD SMALLWOOD
item.description: Iron Maiden’s first real step onto the global stage came in 1981, the same year the band dropped Killers and hit the road for their first world tour.

item.title: MIKE PORTNOY Says LARS ULRICH Was a Major Influence: 'He Was More Than Just a Drummer'
item.description: Mike Portnoy, drummer for progressive metal band Dream Theater, recently shared that Lars Ulrich of Metallica had a big impact on his career, and not just behind the drum kit.

item.title: DAVID ELLEFSON Says DAVE MUSTAINE ‘Hated Playing Before SLAYER’ On 2010 Tour
item.description: Dave Mustaine wasn’t happy with his spot on the lineup during MEGADETH’s tours with SLAYER, according to former bandmate David Ellefson. In a recent episode of The David Ellefson Show podcast (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), the former MEGADETH bassist spoke about the 2010 Jägermeister Music Tour.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: The Night SLASH Felt Deep Shame Over GUNS N’ ROSES’ Treatment of METALLICA: 'I Lost Their Respect'
item.description: Back in the early ’90s, Guns N’ Roses were living the full-throttle rockstar fantasy, loud, chaotic, and unapologetic. Their shows were wild, their image untamed, and their reputation built on pushing limits.

item.title: 5 METALLICA Songs That Have Nothing to Do With HEAVY METAL, Yet WORKED BRILLIANTLY
item.description: Say heavy metal and Metallica instantly comes to mind. Since the early ’80s, the band carved out the sound, fury, and attitude of a genre that lives off shrieking guitars and bone-rattling drums.

item.title: Why Limp Bizkit’s FRED DURST Always Wore That RED BASEBALL CAP
item.description: Back in the early 2000s, nu metal was dominating the rock scene, with bands like Slipknot, Korn, Kid Rock, and Linkin Park in constant rotation on MTV.

item.title: The Heavy METALLICA Song That Tells the Story of JAMES HETFIELD’s Childhood TRAUMA
item.description: James Hetfield, guitarist and frontman of Metallica, didn’t exactly grow up riding rainbows. His early years were marked by the rigid dogma of a household that followed Christian Science, a belief system founded by Lafayette Ronald Hubbard (yep, the same guy behind Scientology).

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD’s Favorite Thrash Bands (That Aren’t METALLICA, SLAYER, MEGADETH or ANTHRAX)
item.description: At this point, saying Metallica “isn’t thrash anymore” is like complaining MTV doesn’t play music videos. Welcome to the last three decades. Sure, the band traded speed for stadiums a while back, but try telling the IRS they’re not the face of thrash metal and see how that goes.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: Ex-Pantera TERRY GLAZE On DIMEBAG's Death: 'It Didn't Hit Me Until I Saw The Dirt'
item.description: Former Pantera vocalist Terry Glaze has shared a personal account of how he learned about the death of guitarist “Dimebag” Darrell Abbott and the emotional aftermath that followed.

item.title: "Thunderstruck," AC/DC Classic, Featured in FIFA Club World Cup Commercial
item.description: AC/DC’s Thunderstruck is the soundtrack for Budweiser’s new commercial. The beer company is a sponsor of the FIFA Club World Cup, which features 32 teams and is currently being held in the United States.

item.title: PIGGY D. On Working With MARILYN MANSON: 'I'm Proud To Stand Next To Him'
item.description: Matt Montgomery, better known as Piggy D., isn’t shy when it comes to describing his experience playing bass for Marilyn Manson. In a recent interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: DUFF MCKAGAN Compares OZZY OSBOURNE to Lemmy, Prince, and Iggy Pop
item.description: Duff McKagan has seen plenty of rock stars come and go, but when it comes to Ozzy Osbourne, he doesn’t mince words. “A constant in rock and roll,” as he puts it.

item.title: DAVE MUSTAINE starts recording vocals as MEGADETH’s 17th studio album nears completion
item.description: The next Megadeth record has been crawling toward completion for months. Since the release of The Sick, The Dying… and the Dead! back in 2022, work on its successor has quietly advanced.

item.title: DAVID VINCENT Reflects On Fan Expectations: 'Nobody Cares About The New Stuff'
item.description: David Vincent, the former Morbid Angel frontman, isn’t exactly rushing to crank out new material with I Am Morbid. In a recent sit-down with Altars Of Metal, the inevitable question popped up: will I Am Morbid ever release original songs?

item.title: David Ellefson: "I Miss Dave" But I’m Done With Megadeth’s Drama
item.description: David Ellefson still feels the absence of Dave Mustaine in his life, even after everything. In a recent chat with The Delz Show, Ellefson reflected: “I miss Dave too.

item.title: Kirk Hammett Rules Out Retirement From Metallica Despite 62 Years of Age
item.description: Kirk Hammett has no interest in slowing down. Speaking to Metal Hammer, he dismissed the idea of retirement entirely. “I don’t believe in retirement. Retirement is something that’s been forced onto people; I don’t believe musicians are allowed to retire,” he said.

item.title: Lzzy Hale Opens Up About New Vocal Mastery After 28 Years Fronting Halestorm
item.description: Long before Lzzy Hale stood under arena lights, she was perched in a dogwood tree somewhere along the Appalachian Trail, testing her voice against the leaves and scaring squirrels.

item.title: Dream Theater’s Mike Portnoy on Pain, Perseverance, and Playing Through Injury
item.description: Step into this scene with me… Dream Theater, mid-’90s, prog-metal gods playing Awake on tour—Portnoy’s behind the kit, hair flailing, sticks a blur, sweat dripping like he’s trying to personally refill the Dead Sea.

item.title: Arch Enemy's Alissa White-Gluz Joins Savage Lands on New Single “Ruling Queen”
item.description: I knew a guy once—swore on his mother’s grave that trees could scream. Not metaphorically, not some poetic nonsense about deforestation being a “cry for help.” No, he meant it literally, said he heard it with his own ears—a deep, resonant moan every time an axe struck bark.

item.title: Ozzy Osbourne “Can’t Walk,” But His Legendary Voice Remains Untouched, Says Sharon
item.description: Alright, so Ozzy Osbourne—THE Prince of Darkness—is out here casually defying medical science. The dude CANNOT WALK. But he CAN STILL BELT OUT “CRAZY TRAIN” LIKE IT’S 1980.

item.title: Meshuggah Drops "Ligature Marks" Music Video Alongside "Immutable - The Indelible Edition" Announcement
item.description: Yep, MESHUGGAH is back to make your speakers beg for mercy—again. Not just playing their usual brand of mind-melting, time-signature-abusing, existential-crisis-inducing metal—oh no, they’ve decided to remaster their already ridiculous 2022 album Immutable and slap on a shiny new title: “Immutable - The Indelible Edition” (because clearly, “Immutable” wasn’t immutable enough).

item.title: Stray From The Path Releases “Kubrick Stare” – A New Single Under SharpTone Records; VIDEO
item.description: Stray From The Path is back. And they’re bringing paranoia with them. Their latest single, “Kubrick Stare”, just dropped (February 5, 2025, mark it) with a music video that’s—well, unsettling, in the best way.

item.title: Ghost Reveals Papa V Perpetua as New Frontman for 2025 World Tour–Everything We Know So Far
item.description: Ah yes. Another day, another Papa. GHOST is back at it again boys, unveiling yet another masked frontman, I mean, why have just one identity when you can cycle through a whole liturgy of them?

item.title: AVENGED SEVENFOLD's M. Shadows Talks God, Purpose, and Fear
item.description: Deep in conversation on the “Artist Friendly With Joel Madden” podcast, the 43-year-old frontman for AVENGED SEVENFOLD, M. Shadows (real name: Matt Sanders), pulled no punches on religion and spirituality.

item.title: Why Tommy Lee Showers Once a Week, According to His Wife
item.description: Tommy Lee, drummer for Mötley Crüe, bathes sparingly. His wife, Brittany Furlan, says he showers only once a week. The detail emerged on Kaitlyn Bristowe’s Off the Vine podcast, where Furlan spoke about her husband’s habits.

item.title: KISS Icon Gene Simmons Speaks Out on Reagan Movie Controversy
item.description: Gene Simmons—yes, the man with the tongue, the fire-breathing antics, and more merchandise than a small country—has added movie soundtrack contributor to his résumé. Recently, he recorded a cover of “Stormy Weather” for the biopic Reagan.

item.title: Creed's First Album Almost Got Shelved Thanks to Conor Oberst
item.description: Back in the mid-’90s, when emo band Commander Venus was trying to make waves, Conor Oberst found himself in an unusual position: previewing Creed’s music before the rest of the world had to deal with it.

item.title: Linkin Park Set to Announce Massive World Tour Ahead of From Zero Release
item.description: Linkin Park’s return to the spotlight hasn’t exactly been smooth sailing. Between the internet losing its collective mind over Emily Armstrong’s connection to Scientology and a convicted r@p1st, the band’s comeback was riding a weird mix of hype and controversy.

item.title: Slipknot’s 2025 European Tour Announced; See Details
item.description: The masters of mayhem in terrifying masks are set to invade Europe again. Slipknot—yes, the band that makes mosh pits feel like a full-contact sport—dropped the news on Instagram about their upcoming 2025 tour.

item.title: As I Lay Dying: Tim Lambesis’ Wife Denies Abuse Claims as Band Falls Apart
item.description: The ongoing collapse of As I Lay Dying is starting to look like the band’s final encore. Over the past week, three members and their manager have jumped ship.

item.title: Drummer Nick Pierce Leaves As I Lay Dying Citing Health Concerns
item.description: As I Lay Dying seems to be unraveling faster than a cheap sweater at a metal merch stand. The band now consists of just Tim Lambesis and Phil Sgrosso, as drummer Nick Pierce becomes the latest member to exit stage left.

item.title: Metallica Returns to Australia and New Zealand This November
item.description: Metallica’s unyielding journey continues, with the band slated to storm Australia and New Zealand next November. This leg of their endless ‘M72 World Tour’ has a lineup that’s sure to turn some heads, featuring Evanescence and Suicidal Tendencies as supporting acts.

item.title: Korn's Original Drummer David Silveria Opens Up on 30th Anniversary
item.description: David Silveria took to Instagram on October 12 to post the cover of the band’s self-titled debut. It wasn’t just a picture, though. He couldn’t resist sharing some heartfelt words.

item.title: Cradle of Filth to Release New Single: Dani Filth Promises Fans Will "Love It"
item.description: Cradle of Filth has once again returned to the spotlight, with frontman Dani Filth making some bold claims about the band’s upcoming single, which is set to drop this October 22.

item.title: Slipknot and Estate of Joey Jordison Settle Lawsuit Quietly
item.description: Joey Jordison’s estate just tied up its legal battle with Slipknot, but good luck trying to find out what really went down. Lawyers on both sides love keeping things as cryptic as possible.

item.title: Slipknot Announces 25th Anniversary Reissue of Debut Album
item.description: The year 1999 gave us Slipknot’s chaotic, self-titled debut—an album that didn’t just make waves; it practically slapped the metal world across the face. Now, 25 years later, they’re not only performing to mark the occasion but teasing what sounds like the mother of all reissues.

item.title: Chester Bennington's Mother Accuses Linkin Park of Betrayal
item.description: The rosy glow of Linkin Park’s reunion announcement didn’t last long, did it? The initial buzz around the band’s so-called “new era”—complete with Emily Armstrong as the replacement vocalist—has quickly turned into a storm of controversy and frustration.

item.title: Emily Armstrong Responds to Scientology and Danny Masterson Allegations
item.description: Oh yeah babe, the music industry—a place where skeletons in closets don’t just rattle, they throw full-blown mosh pits. Barely two days after Linkin Park revealed their shiny new frontwoman, Emily Armstrong (yes, from Dead Sara) found herself in the middle of a PR dumpster fire.

item.title: Slipknot's Sid Wilson Issues Warning After Fire Incident
item.description: Slipknot’s DJ, Sid Wilson, just served up a reminder that fire doesn’t play favorites—or fair. After a recent explosion left him with some nasty burns, he spoke with Fox News about what happened, and it’s a classic tale of human impatience versus nature’s unforgiving tendencies.

item.title: Metallica Pays Tribute to Dedicated Fan Who Died During Edmonton Concert
item.description: Metallica paid a solemn tribute yesterday to one of their own— a dedicated fan, known as Lorne or simply “Viking,” who tragically passed away during their concert in Edmonton, Alberta.

item.title: Sum 41's Deryck Whibley Responds to Linkin Park Frontman Rumors
item.description: Speculation on the rock and metal rumor mill has been churning at full speed this week. Thanks to some coinciding announcements, the internet collectively decided that Sum 41’s frontman, Deryck Whibley, might be stepping in as the new voice of Linkin Park, filling the irreplaceable shoes of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: Slipknot's Sid Wilson Injured in Fire Incident Before Rocklahoma
item.description: Slipknot’s resident turntable wizard, Sid Wilson, found himself trading the spotlight for a hospital bed after a fiery mishap involving an “explosion” left him with burns on his face and arm.

item.title: Slipknot’s 25th Anniversary Kicks Off with Nothing After 1999; VIDEO
item.description: Slipknot has been teasing this nostalgia-heavy tour for what feels like forever, and last night in Noblesville, Indiana, they finally unleashed the beast. Their ‘Here Comes the Pain Tour’ is officially underway, celebrating 25 years of their self-titled debut—a record that pretty much defined what it meant to be an angry, sweaty teenager in the late ’90s.

item.title: Slipknot Revives 1999 Look at Intimate Anniversary Show; VIDEO
item.description: In a tiny California venue better suited for a rowdy karaoke night than the launch of a metal juggernaut’s 25th anniversary, Slipknot made a dramatic entrance. Decked out in those bright red jumpsuits that defined their early days, the band treated the packed crowd at Pappy + Harriet’s in Pioneertown to a full-on blast from the past.

item.title: Korn’s Brian “Head” Welch Fights Back Against Mental Health Struggles
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist of Korn, has recently thrown himself into the mental health arena. He’s teamed up with Atlantic Behavioral Health, a fresh facility in Wilmington, Massachusetts.

item.title: Amy Lee Reflects on Bring Me to Life's Rap: "Not My Style"
item.description: Amy Lee, the unmistakable voice of Evanescence, hasn’t minced words about her feelings toward the now-iconic rap segment in Bring Me to Life. For two decades, she’s openly expressed her discomfort with the label-driven decision to shoehorn in Paul McCoy’s rap—something neither she nor the band originally envisioned for their breakout hit.

item.title: Watch: Exclusive Footage of Metallica's Phantom Lord from Jon Zazula Tribute
item.description: Metallica just dropped official footage of them ripping through Phantom Lord at last weekend’s tribute show for their old manager, Jon Zazula. Yeah, it was one of those nights.
